newsitem.title: USA: CME PORK BELLIES TUMBLE AFTER AUGUST CLIMBED LIMIT.
newsitem.headline: CME PORK BELLIES TUMBLE AFTER AUGUST CLIMBED LIMIT.

text.p: A buy stop placed just above the early low in August CME pork belly futures catapulted that month for a limit gain of 3.000 cents per lb before the contract again fell sharply. Hog futures mostly posted modest gains in light dealings, traders said.
At 1119 CDT, pork bellies were off 1.525 to 0.375 cents with August off most at 81.000 cents. Hog futures were off 0.050 to up 0.300 with August up 0.075 at 80.700 cents.
The buy stop in August bellies was placed when futures were trading lower and the rally came as a surprise, traders said.
August went up the limit before local selling filled the order and turned prices back down. Futures had been pressured early by the recent larger-than-expected setback in cash bellies, they said.
Cash bellies sank $12 per cwt last week after 14-16 lb traded as high as $92 early in the week and then sold as low as $80 on Friday.
Prudential Securities was the buyer in August while Refco bought February early, pit sources said.

Hog futures showed little direction early and generally traded between technical levels. October again slipped to 72.100 cents, chart support, and then recovered to post a gain along with August following expectations of steady to possibly higher cash hog markets Tuesday, traders said.
Hog runs were not as large as expected and packers will have to keep bids strong to draw out enough marketings, they said.
Prudential Securities bought August while Fimat Futures USA and Rand Financials sold, traders said. Rand, locals and buy stops lifted October after Cargill Investor Services sold, pit sources said.
